category_law: Ownership facts below were read from installed package source and confirmed by synthetic execution. None of this is a claim about any real survey file.
subject: Where file opens and reads actually occur in the accepted pyreadstat 1.3.6 runtime

compiled_reader_open_owner.owner: ReadStat C library, compiled into the pyreadstat extension
compiled_reader_open_owner.path_based_behaviour: readstat_parse receives the filename and opens the path itself.
compiled_reader_open_owner.why_python_cannot_see_it: The open happens below the Python C boundary. HQ192 established Python interception cannot observe it and unprivileged DYLD interposition failed on this host. This lane did not repeat those experiments.

broker_seam_discovered.verdict: A broker seam ALREADY EXISTS in the accepted binary. No rebuild is required to reach it.
broker_seam_discovered.mechanism: pyreadstat detects an object exposing .read and .seek, treats it as a file object, and installs four Python-bridging ReadStat handlers.
broker_seam_discovered.critical_consequence: When a file object is supplied, the parser is handed an EMPTY path and the open handler is a no-op. The compiled reader therefore performs no path-level open of its own and has no path available to open.

source_evidence.observation: Both return 0 and do nothing. ReadStat's own open and close of a supplied file object are inert.
Calls the Python object's .read(nbyte) and returns the bytes to ReadStat. An exception raised in the callback is caught and reported to ReadStat as a read failure, returning -1.
Bridges .seek() so ReadStat can reposition within the supplied object.
When file_obj is not None, all four custom handlers are installed and the filename is passed through as an empty string.
The path-based existence check executes ONLY when file_obj is None. It is skipped entirely on the broker route.
if hasattr(filename_path,'read') and hasattr(filename_path,'seek'): file_obj = filename_path; filename_bytes = b''
Pure Python. It forwards the object it is given to read_function repeatedly with row_offset/row_limit. It performs no extension inference and no independent open of its own.
Each entry point hard-sets its parser_format, so the file format is fixed by which function is called and does NOT depend on the path. This is why brokering does not break format selection.

on_the_broker_route.application_open: OWNED BY THE APPLICATION. This is the one and only path-level open in the system, and it is performed before the compiled reader is invoked.
on_the_broker_route.broker_reads: one counted event per read() crossing into the compiled reader
on_the_broker_route.bytes: sum of bytes returned across those reads

ownership_conclusion.measurement_basis: Exact and complete counts at the application-owned file object, not sampling. Every byte the compiled reader consumes passes through a counted read.
ownership_conclusion.why_the_account_is_complete_not_approxim: The reader has no path and an inert open handler. It cannot obtain bytes except by calling the broker's read(). There is no unobserved I/O channel.

prior_lane_relationship.HQ190_C: Established that four mandatory account classes lacked exact bounds in source-free evidence. Not reopened here.
prior_lane_relationship.HQ191: Showed Python reader-layer enforcement working for seven accounts while OS-level opens stayed unobservable. The broker route supplies the missing open account.
prior_lane_relationship.HQ192: Found the Python header-prefix owner and established DYLD was unusable. This lane did not repeat DYLD.
prior_lane_relationship.cross_confirmation: The first brokered metadata read requested exactly 176 bytes, matching the Part C header-prefix size HQ192 identified at the Python layer. This lane observed the same 176-byte prefix arriving from the compiled reader's own read pattern, which is independent corroboration from the opposite direction.
